messages:
Anna Li: quick follow-up from yesterday's obs sync — proposing a lightweight provenance header we can backfill later. idea: keep header tiny for edge clients, carry an opaque token that can be expanded server-side for full lineage.
Raj Patel: sketch it out pls. worried about cost attribution when token resolution is async though.
Anna Li: agreed. basic contract: header `x-rw-pro` (base64, ~24 bytes) with a 1-byte version + 3-5 bytes of flags + 16-byte id. payload kept server-side. example: `x-rw-pro: v1:ABcd12Ef...`
Mike H: curious about how this interacts with sampling. if we drop sampled spans at edge, we lose attribution unless token maps to sampled parent. backfill won't help in that case.
Anna Li: right. proposal: two modes — "hint-only" and "durable-token". hint-only = small provenance fragment in header (service id + local-span-id) for best-effort realtime attribution. durable-token = opaque id that can be looked up to retrieve full envelope later (used by servers and stable SDKs).
Sara G: how do we backfill historical traces? ops needs a plan for bulk enrichment without blowing costs.
Anna Li: backfill plan: incrementally materialize mappings from durable-token->full-attributes during an enrichment job. we start with hot tenants and 7d window. longer tails optional.
Raj Patel: tradeoffs? network overhead vs correctness. also versioning pain when we change attributes schema.
Anna Li: tradeoffs:
- small header: minimal tail latency impact for mobile/edge, but limited realtime fidelity.
- durable token resolution: added lookup cost + potential 100ms tail for attribution queries unless cached.
- backfill: decouples client rollout from server-side indexing but is eventual.
Mike H: could we do a hybrid: include hashed attribute fingerprint in header so cheap realtime grouping works, then full mapping via token for billing accuracy?
Anna Li: exactly what i had in mind. header proto: `v1|flags|fp(8)` + optionally `|tok(16)` for durable. fp=8 bytes fingerprint of tenant+route+model. cheap to index.
Sara G: sounds reasonable. ops checklist?
Raj Patel: list: index design for fp->cost-buckets, cache TTLs, backfill job quotas, migration plan for older SDKs, metrics for missed-attribution rate.
Anna Li: adding: stable HTTP header name, spec in repo, example server-side lookup interface (async) and a sync fallback that attaches best-effort attrs to span.
InfraBot: Reminder: observed enrichment jobs can be scheduled via infra-runner. Use `infra run enrichment-backfill --max-threads=20` to limit blast radius.
Mike H: one more nit — security. opaque token must be HMACed so customers can't forge cross-tenant tokens.
Anna Li: yep: token = HMAC(kms-key, tenant|timestamp|nonce|version) truncated to 16 bytes. include version in header to support rollforward.
Sara G: can we get a quick proto PR? i can take the backfill job spec + quotas.
Anna Li: i'll open a lightweight RFC and a proto PR with header examples and server lookup API today. aim to shepherd through next-week sync. :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: thanks — whoever picks implementation, please add a small perf test showing token-resolve p50/p95 impact.
Anna Li: will do.
Mike H: +1.
Sara G: assigning next steps in the doc.
Anna Li: done — PR incoming.
